In his defence before the court martial (Washington Jan 1848, printed 1848) Fremont states the facts of Jan 1847: 'Governor Stockton gave me an order to re-organize it. General Kearny sent me an order not to re-organize it... I informed General Kearny by letter that I thought he and Governor Stockton ought to adjust the question of rank between themselves: and until that was done I should have to obey Commodore Stockton.' Kearny's testimony (printed there) adds that Fremont 'declined taking it back.' Defiance of a superior general for a rival's order is boldness shown by conduct. The court convicted of mutiny. The cited 1861 arms purchase post-dates 5 March and is dropped.
